summary: Host-local retirement-qualified learner samples conservative resource profiles and brakes pressured admission. Samples persist per execution generation and the estimator reads a bounded trailing window.

replay.detail: One immutable sample row per qualified execution generation is retained, including outside the estimator's trailing window, so replays stay deduplicated.

schema.detail: Local resource_profile_samples_v1 stores host-local sample rows. RequestClass gains the recovery enum value in wire commands and persisted execution/membership state; no graph claim schema changes.

rules.detail: Samples are recorded only in the terminal receipt transaction after confirmed whole-tree retirement; rejected or truncated retirements are not admitted. Recovery admission requires the host profile's recoveryCapable gate and a measured filesystem free-space observation.

compatibility.detail: Recovery is a new wire and persisted RequestClass value. Pre-reader E0 versions reject recovery during Json<Command> extraction, and one persisted recovery execution can fail their whole selected execution-list read. The minimum rollback-reader revision is E0 #6762 at 1a048f9e7946e2a89e6345ca327051e4faca171b, including withdrawal and shell/program-child cancellation fences. Tests at that reader cover lossless unknown-class string roundtrip, a mixed current/future execution list with a recovery refusal code, rejection of unsupported submission/admission/execution update, unchanged synthetic membership state after authority recovery, both shell cancellation selectors retaining cancel=false, and rejected program retirement leaving a live child's status and cancellation-claim index unchanged. They do not prove lossless preservation of every E1 field or an end-to-end live E1-to-E0 rollback. recoveryCapable fences admission only, not decoding. Existing shell_resource_exec, mission_resource_lane and resource_profile_keys health versions do not distinguish E1 recovery support from E0; there is no automatic mixed-version negotiation for this enum.

downtime.detail: No host deployment or caller cutover is activated by this change.

manual.detail: In a mixed fleet, deploy at least E0 1a048f9e7946e2a89e6345ca327051e4faca171b to hosts and clients that may read recovery state before enabling E1 writers. Upgrade an execution host to E1 before routing recovery commands there; keep recoveryCapable disabled until then, and do not use existing health capability versions as proof of recovery support. Older hosts must continue receiving only previously supported classes.

recovery.detail: Retained sample rows provide permanent replay dedupe. Do not roll recovery state back to pre-reader E0 versions; the minimum rollback reader is 1a048f9e7946e2a89e6345ca327051e4faca171b. Its tested guarantees are the class-string/readability and refusal behaviors listed under compatibility, not complete preservation of E1 execution metadata or continued E1 recovery semantics. The synthetic authority-recovery test leaves that membership unchanged; cancellation tests cover the two shell selectors and program membership retirement before linked-child cancellation, not every possible mission lifecycle operation. Unsupported-class restart and background cleanup paths log diagnostics and defer reconciliation; this is not a live rollback certification. Preserve the original state and upgrade forward to E1 for supported reconciliation. Reclamation of samples outside the trailing window remains separate retention debt.
